```{r global-options, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)
```

This document is the single source of truth for every analysis, table, and
figure reported in the manuscript. It reads the prepared inputs, applies the
two motion-exclusion rules, builds the analytic datasets, fits every inferential
model, runs the magnitude bootstrap, and renders every manuscript figure, in
one pass from top to bottom, written out sequentially rather than hidden
behind helper functions. Nothing reported in the manuscript is computed
anywhere else.

Two helper files hold code that is purely mechanical repetition rather than
analysis -- the 5,000-draw bootstrap resampling loop (`R/bootstrap.R`) and the
ggplot/gtable construction for the two figures (`R/plot_helpers.R`). Both are
long and fiddly for reasons that have nothing to do with the statistics, so
they are kept out of the way; everything else -- the raw-data inclusion
rules, the motion-exclusion rules, the person-mean age decomposition, the
modality contrasts, every model formula, and every manuscript table -- is
written out directly below, one rule (primary, then liberal) at a time.

# Setup

```{r setup}
required_packages <- c("here", "tidyverse", "lme4", "lmerTest", "ggh4x", "gtable", "scales")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Install these packages before running this document: ",
       paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(here)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(ggh4x)
  library(grid)   # textGrob()/nullGrob(), used by R/plot_helpers.R
})

# here() searches upward from the working directory for MiND-Reliability.Rproj,
# so every path below is relative to the project root regardless of whether
# this document is knit, run(), or stepped through interactively -- no
# absolute local paths anywhere in this document.
RAW_DATA_DIR <- here("data", "raw")
TABLE_DIR <- here("output", "tables")
FIGURE_DIR <- here("output", "figures")
dir.create(TABLE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(FIGURE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The manuscript specification, fixed here and used everywhere below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
OUTCOMES <- c("Distinctiveness", "Reliability", "Confusability")
MODEL_TERMS <- c("within_cAge", "between_cAge", "Sex_M1", "Education", "aud_mot", "aud_vis")
AGE_TERMS <- c("between_cAge", "within_cAge")
OLDER_ADULT_AGE <- 65          # between_cAge is centred here

RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY <- "FD 0.4 mm / 10% (primary)"
RULE_LABEL_LIBERAL <- "FD 0.5 mm / 20% (liberal)"

MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS <- 5000L
MAGNITUDE_BOOT_SEED <- 20260910L

source(here("R", "bootstrap.R"))     # participant-cluster bootstrap helper
source(here("R", "plot_helpers.R"))  # ggplot construction for Figures 2/3/S1/S2
```

# Load prepared inputs

Exactly four files are read from `data/raw/`, and nothing else. These are
prepared manuscript-analysis inputs, not scanner-level neuroimaging data.
Upstream MRI preprocessing and preparation of these files are outside this
repository's implemented scope; see `data/README.md` for field definitions
and provenance limitations. No study master sheet is read by this analysis.

```{r load-raw-inputs}
required_raw_files <- c(
  "df_mind_all_mc04.csv", "df_mind_all.csv",
  "motion_exclusion_by_run_4mm.csv", "motion_exclusion_by_run_5mm.csv"
)
missing_files <- required_raw_files[
  !file.exists(file.path(RAW_DATA_DIR, required_raw_files))
]
if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop("Missing required raw files in ", RAW_DATA_DIR, ": ",
       paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

# num_threads = 1 is deliberate: the multi-threaded readr parser segfaults on
# these files.
#
# df_mind_all_mc04.csv is outcomes from the FD 0.4 mm scrubbing pipeline (used
# by the primary rule); df_mind_all.csv is the FD 0.5 mm pipeline (liberal
# rule). Each is keyed to the run-level motion file at the matching cutoff.
outcomes_raw_fd04 <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(RAW_DATA_DIR, "df_mind_all_mc04.csv"), num_threads = 1, show_col_types = FALSE
)
outcomes_raw_fd05 <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(RAW_DATA_DIR, "df_mind_all.csv"), num_threads = 1, show_col_types = FALSE
)
motion_fd04 <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(RAW_DATA_DIR, "motion_exclusion_by_run_4mm.csv"), num_threads = 1, show_col_types = FALSE
)
motion_fd05 <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(RAW_DATA_DIR, "motion_exclusion_by_run_5mm.csv"), num_threads = 1, show_col_types = FALSE
)

cat(sprintf(
  "Read %d + %d outcome rows and %d + %d motion records from data/raw/.\n",
  nrow(outcomes_raw_fd04), nrow(outcomes_raw_fd05), nrow(motion_fd04), nrow(motion_fd05)
))
```

# Construct analysis datasets

Each outcome file is wide (one `{Modality}{Outcome}` column per
modality-outcome pair); it is reshaped to one row per subject x wave x
modality. Wave 3 is dropped here, before any motion accounting, so every
later count is Waves 1-2 only -- the exploratory three-wave MIND-C analysis is
not part of this manuscript. The primary and liberal outcome files are
reshaped separately and identically, since they feed two different motion
rules below.

```{r reshape-outcomes}
outcomes_long_fd04 <- outcomes_raw_fd04 %>%
  filter(!is.na(SubNum)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(Aud|Mot|Vis)(Distinctiveness|Reliability|Confusability)$"),
    names_to = c("Modality", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(Aud|Mot|Vis)(.*)"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Modality = factor(Modality, levels = c("Aud", "Mot", "Vis"))) %>%
  filter(Wave_Num %in% c(1, 2))

outcomes_long_fd05 <- outcomes_raw_fd05 %>%
  filter(!is.na(SubNum)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(Aud|Mot|Vis)(Distinctiveness|Reliability|Confusability)$"),
    names_to = c("Modality", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(Aud|Mot|Vis)(.*)"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Modality = factor(Modality, levels = c("Aud", "Mot", "Vis"))) %>%
  filter(Wave_Num %in% c(1, 2))

# Subgroup == 1 identifies the healthy-subject cohort the manuscript analyzes.
# Both outcome files describe the same participants, so this is the same ID
# set either way; both are combined defensively.
healthy_subject_ids <- bind_rows(outcomes_long_fd04, outcomes_long_fd05) %>%
  filter(Subgroup == 1) %>%
  distinct(Subject) %>%
  pull(Subject)

# Used only for Table S3 (motion accounting), which breaks runs assessed down
# by age group.
subject_age_groups <- bind_rows(outcomes_long_fd04, outcomes_long_fd05) %>%
  filter(Subgroup == 1) %>%
  distinct(Subject, Age_DuringParticipation_) %>%
  transmute(
    Subject,
    Age_Group = factor(
      if_else(Age_DuringParticipation_ < OLDER_ADULT_AGE, "Young adults", "Older adults"),
      levels = c("Young adults", "Older adults")
    )
  )

cat(sprintf("%d healthy-cohort participants (Subgroup == 1).\n", length(healthy_subject_ids)))
```

# Motion exclusion and accounting

Two motion-exclusion rules are applied to the run-level motion file at the
matching FD cutoff:

| Rule    | FD cutoff | Run excluded at |
| ------- | --------- | ---------------- |
| primary | 0.4 mm    | >= 10% scrubbed volumes |
| liberal | 0.5 mm    | >= 20% scrubbed volumes |

A run is identified by subject x modality x session (`placebo`) x run
(`001`); only the healthy cohort's assessed runs are considered.

```{r build-run-flags}
run_flags_primary <- motion_fd04 %>%
  filter(
    subject %in% healthy_subject_ids,
    session == "placebo",
    run == "001",
    experiment %in% c("auditory", "visual", "motor")
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Subject = subject,
    Modality = recode(experiment, auditory = "Aud", motor = "Mot", visual = "Vis"),
    pct_excluded,
    exclude = pct_excluded >= 10
  )

run_flags_liberal <- motion_fd05 %>%
  filter(
    subject %in% healthy_subject_ids,
    session == "placebo",
    run == "001",
    experiment %in% c("auditory", "visual", "motor")
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Subject = subject,
    Modality = recode(experiment, auditory = "Aud", motor = "Mot", visual = "Vis"),
    pct_excluded,
    exclude = pct_excluded >= 20
  )
```

Joining outcomes to motion flags can leave a subject x modality row with NO
matching motion record at all (`exclude` is `NA`, not `FALSE`). This handling
has already been audited (see the note below) and is preserved exactly: a
row with no run-level motion record is DROPPED, not retained. `!exclude`
already drops `NA`, but the `!is.na(exclude)` test is written out so the
intent is explicit.

```{r apply-motion-rule}
# Wave-1/2 outcome rows are joined before motion exclusion for the diagnostic
# below. Run flags already use healthy-cohort IDs; Subgroup == 1 is applied
# explicitly to joined rows when building the analytic datasets.
joined_fd04 <- outcomes_long_fd04 %>% left_join(run_flags_primary, by = c("Subject", "Modality"))
joined_fd05 <- outcomes_long_fd05 %>% left_join(run_flags_liberal, by = c("Subject", "Modality"))

missing_motion_primary <- joined_fd04 %>% filter(Subgroup == 1, is.na(exclude))
missing_motion_liberal <- joined_fd05 %>% filter(Subgroup == 1, is.na(exclude))

cat(sprintf(
  "Unmatched subject x modality x wave rows with no motion record: %d (primary), %d (liberal).\n",
  nrow(missing_motion_primary), nrow(missing_motion_liberal)
))
cat(
  "These rows are excluded, not recovered or added: all three prepared outcomes\n",
  "are already absent for them under both rules, so admitting them would not\n",
  "add complete model observations. This policy and the join are unchanged\n",
  "from the audited analysis.\n"
)
```

Table S3 (motion accounting: runs assessed and excluded, by age group and
modality) is built from the assessed run-flag sets, before excluded runs are
removed. Those sets already use healthy-cohort IDs from Waves 1-2. Its
construction is deferred to the Tables section below, alongside the other
manuscript tables.

# Age decomposition

The corrected person-mean decomposition is preserved exactly. Mean age is
computed over **unique retained participant-wave observations**, not
modality-level rows, so the number of modalities retained at a wave cannot
influence a participant's mean age:

```
age_by_wave <- distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_)
mean_age    <- mean(Age_DuringParticipation_)        # per participant
between_cAge <- mean_age - 65
within_cAge  <- Age_DuringParticipation_ - mean_age  # per wave
```

A one-wave participant therefore has `within_cAge == 0`; a participant
observed at ages 70 and 74 has `mean_age = 72` and within-person ages -2 and
+2, regardless of how many modalities survived motion exclusion at either
wave. A worked example, checked before this is ever applied to real data:

```{r age-decomposition-worked-example}
worked_example <- tibble(
  SubNum = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2),
  Wave_Num = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2),
  Age_DuringParticipation_ = c(70, 70, 70, 74, 60, 60),
  Modality = c("Aud", "Mot", "Vis", "Aud", "Aud", "Vis")
)

worked_example_age_by_wave <- worked_example %>%
  distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_) %>%
  group_by(SubNum) %>%
  mutate(mean_age = mean(Age_DuringParticipation_), n_waves = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    between_cAge = mean_age - OLDER_ADULT_AGE,
    within_cAge = Age_DuringParticipation_ - mean_age
  )

worked_example_checked <- worked_example %>%
  left_join(
    worked_example_age_by_wave %>%
      select(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_, mean_age, within_cAge, between_cAge, n_waves),
    by = c("SubNum", "Wave_Num", "Age_DuringParticipation_")
  )
stopifnot(
  all(worked_example_checked$mean_age[worked_example_checked$SubNum == 1] == 72),
  identical(worked_example_checked$within_cAge, c(-2, -2, -2, 2, 0, 0))
)

# Dropping a modality at a retained wave must not move that wave's age terms,
# because mean age above is computed from distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age) --
# before any modality-level row is ever counted.
worked_example_subset <- worked_example[c(1, 4, 5), ]
worked_example_subset_age_by_wave <- worked_example_subset %>%
  distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_) %>%
  group_by(SubNum) %>%
  mutate(mean_age = mean(Age_DuringParticipation_), n_waves = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    between_cAge = mean_age - OLDER_ADULT_AGE,
    within_cAge = Age_DuringParticipation_ - mean_age
  )
worked_example_subset_checked <- worked_example_subset %>%
  left_join(
    worked_example_subset_age_by_wave %>%
      select(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_, mean_age, within_cAge, between_cAge, n_waves),
    by = c("SubNum", "Wave_Num", "Age_DuringParticipation_")
  )
stopifnot(identical(
  worked_example_subset_checked$within_cAge,
  worked_example_checked$within_cAge[c(1, 4, 5)]
))
cat("Worked example passed: mean age 72 for participant 1 (ages 70, 74); within-person ages -2/+2.\n")
```

Applied to the motion-filtered data, primary rule:

```{r age-decomposition-primary}
analysis_primary <- joined_fd04 %>%
  filter(!is.na(exclude), !exclude, Subgroup == 1)

age_by_wave_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_)
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(age_by_wave_primary),
  !anyDuplicated(age_by_wave_primary[c("SubNum", "Wave_Num")])
)

age_by_wave_primary <- age_by_wave_primary %>%
  group_by(SubNum) %>%
  mutate(mean_age = mean(Age_DuringParticipation_), n_waves = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    between_cAge = mean_age - OLDER_ADULT_AGE,
    within_cAge = Age_DuringParticipation_ - mean_age
  )

# Invariants the decomposition must satisfy: a one-wave participant has zero
# within-person age; a participant's within-person ages sum to zero around
# their own mean; between_cAge is a simple re-centring of mean_age and
# nothing else.
within_sums_primary <- tapply(age_by_wave_primary$within_cAge, age_by_wave_primary$SubNum, sum)
stopifnot(
  all(age_by_wave_primary$within_cAge[age_by_wave_primary$n_waves == 1] == 0),
  all(abs(within_sums_primary) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(age_by_wave_primary$between_cAge - (age_by_wave_primary$mean_age - OLDER_ADULT_AGE)) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(age_by_wave_primary$within_cAge -
    (age_by_wave_primary$Age_DuringParticipation_ - age_by_wave_primary$mean_age)) < 1e-9)
)

n_rows_before_age_join_primary <- nrow(analysis_primary)
analysis_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  left_join(
    age_by_wave_primary %>%
      select(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_, mean_age, within_cAge, between_cAge, n_waves),
    by = c("SubNum", "Wave_Num", "Age_DuringParticipation_")
  )
stopifnot(nrow(analysis_primary) == n_rows_before_age_join_primary)
```

Applied to the motion-filtered data, liberal rule (identical steps):

```{r age-decomposition-liberal}
analysis_liberal <- joined_fd05 %>%
  filter(!is.na(exclude), !exclude, Subgroup == 1)

age_by_wave_liberal <- analysis_liberal %>%
  distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_)
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(age_by_wave_liberal),
  !anyDuplicated(age_by_wave_liberal[c("SubNum", "Wave_Num")])
)

age_by_wave_liberal <- age_by_wave_liberal %>%
  group_by(SubNum) %>%
  mutate(mean_age = mean(Age_DuringParticipation_), n_waves = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    between_cAge = mean_age - OLDER_ADULT_AGE,
    within_cAge = Age_DuringParticipation_ - mean_age
  )

within_sums_liberal <- tapply(age_by_wave_liberal$within_cAge, age_by_wave_liberal$SubNum, sum)
stopifnot(
  all(age_by_wave_liberal$within_cAge[age_by_wave_liberal$n_waves == 1] == 0),
  all(abs(within_sums_liberal) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(age_by_wave_liberal$between_cAge - (age_by_wave_liberal$mean_age - OLDER_ADULT_AGE)) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(age_by_wave_liberal$within_cAge -
    (age_by_wave_liberal$Age_DuringParticipation_ - age_by_wave_liberal$mean_age)) < 1e-9)
)

n_rows_before_age_join_liberal <- nrow(analysis_liberal)
analysis_liberal <- analysis_liberal %>%
  left_join(
    age_by_wave_liberal %>%
      select(SubNum, Wave_Num, Age_DuringParticipation_, mean_age, within_cAge, between_cAge, n_waves),
    by = c("SubNum", "Wave_Num", "Age_DuringParticipation_")
  )
stopifnot(nrow(analysis_liberal) == n_rows_before_age_join_liberal)
```

# Modality coding

Two numeric contrasts code modality exactly as specified, so a model with
both terms estimates Auditory, Motor, and Visual as distinct levels without a
factor:

```{r modality-coding}
analysis_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  mutate(
    aud_mot = case_when(Modality == "Aud" ~ -1, Modality == "Mot" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0),
    aud_vis = case_when(Modality == "Aud" ~ -1, Modality == "Vis" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  )

analysis_liberal <- analysis_liberal %>%
  mutate(
    aud_mot = case_when(Modality == "Aud" ~ -1, Modality == "Mot" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0),
    aud_vis = case_when(Modality == "Aud" ~ -1, Modality == "Vis" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  )

stopifnot(
  all(analysis_primary$aud_mot[analysis_primary$Modality == "Aud"] == -1),
  all(analysis_primary$aud_mot[analysis_primary$Modality == "Mot"] == 1),
  all(analysis_primary$aud_mot[analysis_primary$Modality == "Vis"] == 0),
  all(analysis_primary$aud_vis[analysis_primary$Modality == "Aud"] == -1),
  all(analysis_primary$aud_vis[analysis_primary$Modality == "Vis"] == 1),
  all(analysis_primary$aud_vis[analysis_primary$Modality == "Mot"] == 0)
)
```

# Sample checks

Sample sizes are checked against the validated reference at commit
`25118f0b5bcad8c08bc1b40865b1870c3bbb39db` as a regression check: if the
raw inputs or the exclusion logic ever changed, these counts would move and
this chunk would fail. `returner_ids_primary`/`returner_ids_liberal` computed
here are reused below when the Wave-1-anchored table samples are built.

```{r sample-checks-primary}
session_rows_primary <- analysis_primary %>% distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num)
wave1_ids_primary <- session_rows_primary$SubNum[session_rows_primary$Wave_Num == 1]
wave2_ids_primary <- session_rows_primary$SubNum[session_rows_primary$Wave_Num == 2]
returner_ids_primary <- intersect(wave1_ids_primary, wave2_ids_primary)

n_observations_primary <- nrow(analysis_primary)
n_sessions_primary <- nrow(session_rows_primary)
n_participants_primary <- n_distinct(analysis_primary$SubNum)
n_returners_primary <- length(returner_ids_primary)
n_wave1_sessions_primary <- sum(session_rows_primary$Wave_Num == 1)
n_wave2_sessions_primary <- sum(session_rows_primary$Wave_Num == 2)
n_wave2_only_primary <- length(setdiff(wave2_ids_primary, wave1_ids_primary))

cat(sprintf(
  "Primary: %d observations, %d sessions, %d participants, %d returners, %d Wave-1 sessions, %d Wave-2 sessions, %d Wave-2-only participants.\n",
  n_observations_primary, n_sessions_primary, n_participants_primary, n_returners_primary,
  n_wave1_sessions_primary, n_wave2_sessions_primary, n_wave2_only_primary
))

stopifnot(
  n_observations_primary == 724,
  n_sessions_primary == 276,
  n_participants_primary == 218,
  n_returners_primary == 58,
  n_wave1_sessions_primary == 217,
  n_wave2_sessions_primary == 59,
  n_wave2_only_primary == 1
)
```

```{r sample-checks-liberal}
session_rows_liberal <- analysis_liberal %>% distinct(SubNum, Wave_Num)
wave1_ids_liberal <- session_rows_liberal$SubNum[session_rows_liberal$Wave_Num == 1]
wave2_ids_liberal <- session_rows_liberal$SubNum[session_rows_liberal$Wave_Num == 2]
returner_ids_liberal <- intersect(wave1_ids_liberal, wave2_ids_liberal)

n_observations_liberal <- nrow(analysis_liberal)
n_sessions_liberal <- nrow(session_rows_liberal)
n_participants_liberal <- n_distinct(analysis_liberal$SubNum)
n_returners_liberal <- length(returner_ids_liberal)
n_wave1_sessions_liberal <- sum(session_rows_liberal$Wave_Num == 1)
n_wave2_sessions_liberal <- sum(session_rows_liberal$Wave_Num == 2)
n_wave2_only_liberal <- length(setdiff(wave2_ids_liberal, wave1_ids_liberal))

cat(sprintf(
  "Liberal: %d observations, %d sessions, %d participants, %d returners, %d Wave-1 sessions, %d Wave-2 sessions, %d Wave-2-only participants.\n",
  n_observations_liberal, n_sessions_liberal, n_participants_liberal, n_returners_liberal,
  n_wave1_sessions_liberal, n_wave2_sessions_liberal, n_wave2_only_liberal
))

stopifnot(
  n_observations_liberal == 841,
  n_sessions_liberal == 286,
  n_participants_liberal == 226,
  n_returners_liberal == 60,
  n_wave1_sessions_liberal == 226,
  n_wave2_sessions_liberal == 60,
  n_wave2_only_liberal == 0
)
cat("Sample sizes match the audited analysis for both rules.\n")
```

# Manuscript tables

Manuscript groups are **Wave-1-anchored**: a participant retained only at
Wave 2 (the primary rule's one Wave-2-only older adult) remains in the
analytic models but is deliberately absent from these demographic groups.
Four samples are defined per rule, reused by both Table 1/S1 (participant
characteristics) and Table 3/S2 (descriptive statistics):

```{r sample-subsets-primary}
young_wave1_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  filter(Wave_Num == 1, Age_DuringParticipation_ < OLDER_ADULT_AGE)
older_wave1_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  filter(Wave_Num == 1, Age_DuringParticipation_ >= OLDER_ADULT_AGE)
older_wave2_returners_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  filter(Wave_Num == 2, Age_DuringParticipation_ >= OLDER_ADULT_AGE, SubNum %in% returner_ids_primary)
older_wave1_returners_primary <- older_wave1_primary %>%
  filter(SubNum %in% returner_ids_primary)
```

```{r sample-subsets-liberal}
young_wave1_liberal <- analysis_liberal %>%
  filter(Wave_Num == 1, Age_DuringParticipation_ < OLDER_ADULT_AGE)
older_wave1_liberal <- analysis_liberal %>%
  filter(Wave_Num == 1, Age_DuringParticipation_ >= OLDER_ADULT_AGE)
older_wave2_returners_liberal <- analysis_liberal %>%
  filter(Wave_Num == 2, Age_DuringParticipation_ >= OLDER_ADULT_AGE, SubNum %in% returner_ids_liberal)
older_wave1_returners_liberal <- older_wave1_liberal %>%
  filter(SubNum %in% returner_ids_liberal)
```

## Table 1 -- primary participant characteristics

Each row below is one participant-level sample, deduplicated to one row per
participant before summarising age/education/sex.

```{r table-1}
young_wave1_primary_participants <- young_wave1_primary %>% distinct(SubNum, .keep_all = TRUE)
older_wave1_primary_participants <- older_wave1_primary %>% distinct(SubNum, .keep_all = TRUE)
older_wave2_returners_primary_participants <- older_wave2_returners_primary %>% distinct(SubNum, .keep_all = TRUE)
older_wave1_returners_primary_participants <- older_wave1_returners_primary %>% distinct(SubNum, .keep_all = TRUE)

table_1_young_wave1 <- tibble(
  motion_rule = RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY,
  sample = "Young adults, Wave 1",
  n = nrow(young_wave1_primary_participants),
  age_m = mean(young_wave1_primary_participants$Age_DuringParticipation_, na.rm = TRUE),
  age_sd = sd(young_wave1_primary_participants$Age_DuringParticipation_, na.rm = TRUE),
  age_min = min(young_wave1_primary_participants$Age_DuringParticipation_, na.rm = TRUE),
  age_max = max(young_wave1_primary_participants$Age_DuringParticipation_, na.rm = TRUE),
  education_m = mean(young_wave1_primary_participants$Education, na.rm = TRUE),
  education_sd = sd(young_wave1_primary_participants$Education, na.rm = TRUE),
  n_men = sum(young_wave1_primary_participants$Sex_M1 == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
  n_women = sum(young_wave1_primary_participants$Sex_M1 == 2, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

## Table S3 -- motion accounting

Runs assessed/excluded by age group and modality, both rules, plus the
age-group, modality, and grand-total aggregates. Built from the full
assessed run-flag sets before motion exclusion, joined to each subject's age
group. These sets already use healthy-cohort IDs from Waves 1-2.

```{r table-s3}
flags_primary <- run_flags_primary %>%
  left_join(subject_age_groups, by = "Subject") %>%
  mutate(
    age_group = as.character(Age_Group),
    modality = recode(as.character(Modality), Aud = "Auditory", Mot = "Motor", Vis = "Visual")
  )

motion_primary_by_age_modality <- flags_primary %>%
  group_by(age_group, modality) %>%
  summarise(
    runs_assessed = n(), runs_excluded = sum(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_runs_excluded = 100 * mean(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pct_volumes_scrubbed = mean(pct_excluded, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"
  )
motion_primary_by_age <- flags_primary %>%
  group_by(age_group) %>%
  summarise(
    runs_assessed = n(), runs_excluded = sum(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_runs_excluded = 100 * mean(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pct_volumes_scrubbed = mean(pct_excluded, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(modality = "All modalities")
motion_primary_by_modality <- flags_primary %>%
  group_by(modality) %>%
  summarise(
    runs_assessed = n(), runs_excluded = sum(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_runs_excluded = 100 * mean(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pct_volumes_scrubbed = mean(pct_excluded, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(age_group = "All participants")
motion_primary_overall <- flags_primary %>%
  summarise(
    runs_assessed = n(), runs_excluded = sum(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_runs_excluded = 100 * mean(exclude, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pct_volumes_scrubbed = mean(pct_excluded, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(age_group = "All participants", modality = "All modalities")

table_s3_primary <- bind_rows(
  motion_primary_by_age_modality, motion_primary_by_age,
  motion_primary_by_modality, motion_primary_overall
) %>%
  mutate(motion_rule = RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY, .before = 1) %>%
  select(motion_rule, age_group, modality, runs_assessed, runs_excluded, pct_runs_excluded, mean_pct_volumes_scrubbed)

  left_join(subject_age_groups, by = "Subject") %>%

  )

  )
motion_liberal_by_age <- flags_liberal %>%

  summarise(
```

# Primary mixed-effects models

The manuscript's inferential specification, fit separately for each outcome
under the primary motion rule. `lmerTest::lmer()`, `REML = FALSE`,
Satterthwaite degrees of freedom and p-values throughout; `car::Anova()` is
not used for manuscript inference anywhere in this document.

```{r primary-models}
model_data_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  drop_na(all_of(c(OUTCOMES, MODEL_TERMS, "SubNum")))

model_primary_distinctiveness <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Distinctiveness ~ within_cAge + between_cAge + Sex_M1 + Education + aud_mot + aud_vis + (1 | SubNum),
  data = model_data_primary, REML = FALSE
)
summary(model_primary_distinctiveness)

model_primary_reliability <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Reliability ~ within_cAge + between_cAge + Sex_M1 + Education + aud_mot + aud_vis + (1 | SubNum),
  data = model_data_primary, REML = FALSE
)
summary(model_primary_reliability)

model_primary_confusability <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Confusability ~ within_cAge + between_cAge + Sex_M1 + Education + aud_mot + aud_vis + (1 | SubNum),
  data = model_data_primary, REML = FALSE
)
summary(model_primary_confusability)
```

## Table 2 -- primary fixed effects

Extracted directly from the three models above; one block per outcome, then
stacked.

```{r table-2}
coef_primary_distinctiveness <- summary(model_primary_distinctiveness, ddf = "Satterthwaite")$coefficients
table_2_distinctiveness <- tibble(
  motion_rule = RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY,
  outcome = "Distinctiveness",
  term = rownames(coef_primary_distinctiveness),
  estimate = coef_primary_distinctiveness[, "Estimate"],
  se = coef_primary_distinctiveness[, "Std. Error"],
  df = coef_primary_distinctiveness[, "df"],
  t = coef_primary_distinctiveness[, "t value"],
  p = coef_primary_distinctiveness[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
  n_observations = nrow(model_primary_distinctiveness@frame),
  n_participants = n_distinct(model_primary_distinctiveness@frame$SubNum)
)

coef_primary_reliability <- summary(model_primary_reliability, ddf = "Satterthwaite")$coefficients
table_2_reliability <- tibble(
  motion_rule = RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY,
  outcome = "Reliability",
  term = rownames(coef_primary_reliability),
  estimate = coef_primary_reliability[, "Estimate"],
  se = coef_primary_reliability[, "Std. Error"],
  df = coef_primary_reliability[, "df"],
  t = coef_primary_reliability[, "t value"],
  p = coef_primary_reliability[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
  n_observations = nrow(model_primary_reliability@frame),
  n_participants = n_distinct(model_primary_reliability@frame$SubNum)
)

coef_primary_confusability <- summary(model_primary_confusability, ddf = "Satterthwaite")$coefficients
table_2_confusability <- tibble(
  motion_rule = RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY,
  outcome = "Confusability",
  term = rownames(coef_primary_confusability),
  estimate = coef_primary_confusability[, "Estimate"],
  se = coef_primary_confusability[, "Std. Error"],
  df = coef_primary_confusability[, "df"],
  t = coef_primary_confusability[, "t value"],
  p = coef_primary_confusability[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
  n_observations = nrow(model_primary_confusability@frame),
  n_participants = n_distinct(model_primary_confusability@frame$SubNum)
)

table_2 <- bind_rows(table_2_distinctiveness, table_2_reliability, table_2_confusability)
write_csv(table_2, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "table_2.csv"))
table_2
```

```{r liberal-models}
  Reliability ~ within_cAge + between_cAge + Sex_M1 + Education + aud_mot + aud_vis + (1 | SubNum),

)

  data = model_data_liberal, REML = FALSE
)
summary(model_liberal_confusability)
```

# Participant-level magnitude bootstrap

For both motion rules:

```
delta = |beta_Reliability| - |beta_Confusability|
```

for the between-person and within-person age terms separately, using
participant-level cluster resampling (5,000 draws, seed 20260910): every
retained wave/modality belonging to a sampled participant travels together,
and each duplicated copy of a resampled participant gets a fresh cluster ID
so it contributes an independent random-intercept level. The Reliability and
Confusability models are refit within every draw and the 95% CI is the
percentile interval of the resulting `delta` draws. A singular fit (a
participant variance at the zero boundary) remains eligible and is retained,
not discarded -- see `R/bootstrap.R` for why. The resampling loop itself
lives there; the formula it refits is the one fit visibly above.

```{r magnitude-bootstrap}
boot_cores <- magnitude_boot_cores()
cat("Bootstrapping with", boot_cores, "worker(s); B =", MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS,
    "; seed =", MAGNITUDE_BOOT_SEED, "\n")

boot_primary <- magnitude_bootstrap(
  model_data_primary, AGE_TERMS,
  B = MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS, seed = MAGNITUDE_BOOT_SEED, cores = boot_cores
)
cat(sprintf(
  "Primary: %d/%d draws singular (retained); %d/%d usable per age term.\n",
  sum(boot_primary$singular_draws), MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS,
  min(boot_primary$summary$n_boot_ok), MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS
))

boot_liberal <- magnitude_bootstrap(
  model_data_liberal, AGE_TERMS,
  B = MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS, seed = MAGNITUDE_BOOT_SEED, cores = boot_cores
)
cat(sprintf(
  "Liberal: %d/%d draws singular (retained); %d/%d usable per age term.\n",
  sum(boot_liberal$singular_draws), MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS,
  min(boot_liberal$summary$n_boot_ok), MAGNITUDE_BOOT_DRAWS
))
```

The bootstrap refits the identical formula on the identical data, so its
point estimates must reproduce the pooled Reliability/Confusability slopes
in Tables 2/S4 exactly (to floating-point noise):

```{r check-bootstrap-point-estimates}
stopifnot(
  abs(boot_primary$point$b_reliability[boot_primary$point$age_term == "between_cAge"] -
      table_2$estimate[table_2$outcome == "Reliability" & table_2$term == "between_cAge"]) < 1e-8,
  abs(boot_primary$point$b_reliability[boot_primary$point$age_term == "within_cAge"] -
      table_2$estimate[table_2$outcome == "Reliability" & table_2$term == "within_cAge"]) < 1e-8,
  abs(boot_primary$point$b_confusability[boot_primary$point$age_term == "between_cAge"] -
      table_2$estimate[table_2$outcome == "Confusability" & table_2$term == "between_cAge"]) < 1e-8,
  abs(boot_primary$point$b_confusability[boot_primary$point$age_term == "within_cAge"] -
      table_2$estimate[table_2$outcome == "Confusability" & table_2$term == "within_cAge"]) < 1e-8
)
stopifnot(
  abs(boot_liberal$point$b_reliability[boot_liberal$point$age_term == "between_cAge"] -
      table_s4$estimate[table_s4$outcome == "Reliability" & table_s4$term == "between_cAge"]) < 1e-8,
  abs(boot_liberal$point$b_reliability[boot_liberal$point$age_term == "within_cAge"] -
      table_s4$estimate[table_s4$outcome == "Reliability" & table_s4$term == "within_cAge"]) < 1e-8,
  abs(boot_liberal$point$b_confusability[boot_liberal$point$age_term == "between_cAge"] -
      table_s4$estimate[table_s4$outcome == "Confusability" & table_s4$term == "between_cAge"]) < 1e-8,
  abs(boot_liberal$point$b_confusability[boot_liberal$point$age_term == "within_cAge"] -
      table_s4$estimate[table_s4$outcome == "Confusability" & table_s4$term == "within_cAge"]) < 1e-8
)
cat("Bootstrap point estimates match Tables 2/S4 exactly.\n")

magnitude_comparison <- bind_rows(
  boot_primary$summary %>% mutate(motion_rule = RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY, .before = 1),
  boot_liberal$summary %>% mutate(motion_rule = RULE_LABEL_LIBERAL, .before = 1)
)
write_csv(magnitude_comparison, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "magnitude_comparison.csv"))
magnitude_comparison
```

Raw bootstrap draws are saved so the full resampling distribution can be
inspected without rerunning 5,000 iterations per rule:

```{r save-bootstrap-draws}
draws_primary <- as_tibble(boot_primary$draws)
draws_primary <- bind_cols(draw = seq_len(nrow(draws_primary)), draws_primary)
write_csv(draws_primary, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "bootstrap_draws_primary.csv"))

draws_liberal <- as_tibble(boot_liberal$draws)
draws_liberal <- bind_cols(draw = seq_len(nrow(draws_liberal)), draws_liberal)
write_csv(draws_liberal, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "bootstrap_draws_liberal.csv"))
```

# Figure 2

The combined age-effect figure: a 3 x 2 grid, outcome by row (distinctiveness,
reliability, confusability) and age term by column (between-person age,
within-person years from first wave), under the primary motion rule. The
heavy near-black pooled line in every panel comes from the exact model
reported in Table 2. The three colored modality lines are **descriptive
only**, from a VISUALIZATION-ONLY interaction model fit below: they carry no
inferential interaction test, no simple-slope estimate, and no manuscript
conclusion, and the caption does not depend on any interaction p-value.

```{r figure-2-visualization-models}
# VISUALIZATION ONLY. These allow each modality its own age slope purely to
# draw descriptive colored lines; no test on this interaction is computed or
# reported anywhere. contr.sum gives a valid contrast coding for a factor
# inside an interaction; it is set on this copy of the data only; the pooled
# models above (and their contrasts) are untouched.
vis_data_primary <- analysis_primary %>%
  mutate(
    Modality = factor(
      recode(as.character(Modality), Aud = "Auditory", Vis = "Visual", Mot = "Motor"),
      levels = INTERACTION_MODALITY_LEVELS
    )
  ) %>%
  drop_na(all_of(c(OUTCOMES, "between_cAge", "within_cAge", "Sex_M1", "Education", "SubNum", "Modality")))
contrasts(vis_data_primary$Modality) <- "contr.sum"

vis_model_primary_distinctiveness <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Distinctiveness ~ (between_cAge + within_cAge) * Modality + Sex_M1 + Education + (1 | SubNum),
  data = vis_data_primary, REML = FALSE
)
vis_model_primary_reliability <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Reliability ~ (between_cAge + within_cAge) * Modality + Sex_M1 + Education + (1 | SubNum),
  data = vis_data_primary, REML = FALSE
)
vis_model_primary_confusability <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Confusability ~ (between_cAge + within_cAge) * Modality + Sex_M1 + Education + (1 | SubNum),
  data = vis_data_primary, REML = FALSE
)
```

`R/plot_helpers.R`'s figure-building functions take the three models of a
rule as one named list; this is the one place in this document a list of
models is built, because the plotting code needs to look a model up by
outcome name:

```{r figure-2-build, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 7.3}
models_primary <- list(
  Distinctiveness = model_primary_distinctiveness,
  Reliability = model_primary_reliability,
  Confusability = model_primary_confusability
)
vis_models_primary <- list(
  Distinctiveness = vis_model_primary_distinctiveness,
  Reliability = vis_model_primary_reliability,
  Confusability = vis_model_primary_confusability
)

between_person_data_primary <- between_person_plot_data(analysis_primary, models_primary, vis_models_primary)
within_person_data_primary <- within_person_plot_data(analysis_primary, models_primary, vis_models_primary)
combined_lines_primary <- combined_plot_data(between_person_data_primary, within_person_data_primary)

figure_2 <- build_combined_figure(
  combined_lines_primary, combined_pooled_slopes(table_2, RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY), centred = TRUE
)
invisible(verify_combined_figure(figure_2, combined_lines_primary))
figure_2_grob <- add_column_axis_titles(figure_2)
grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(figure_2_grob)

save_manuscript_figure(figure_2_grob, FIGURE_DIR, "figure_2",
                       height_mm = COMBINED_HEIGHT_MM, width_mm = COMBINED_WIDTH_MM)
write_figure_caption(combined_caption("Figure 2", RULE_LABEL_PRIMARY), FIGURE_DIR, "figure_2")
```

# Final validation checks

Independent cross-checks of everything built above, run after the fact so a
regression anywhere in the pipeline is caught here rather than discovered by
a reader.

```{r final-checks}
# The outcome identity holds row-by-row in the analytic data. It is not
# expected to hold between separately fitted model coefficients: each model
# estimates its own covariance parameters.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(analysis_primary$Distinctiveness -
            (analysis_primary$Reliability - analysis_primary$Confusability)) < 1e-8, na.rm = TRUE),
  all(abs(analysis_liberal$Distinctiveness -
            (analysis_liberal$Reliability - analysis_liberal$Confusability)) < 1e-8, na.rm = TRUE)
)
cat("Outcome identity (Distinctiveness = Reliability - Confusability) holds in both analytic datasets.\n")

# Retained Average point summaries are recomputed from session x modality
# observations and compared. These points are not displayed in the current
# figures, whose columns show between-person and within-person model lines.
print_average_check(between_person_average_check(analysis_primary, between_person_data_primary$points))
print_average_check(within_person_average_check(analysis_primary, within_person_data_primary$points))
print_average_check(between_person_average_check(analysis_liberal, between_person_data_liberal$points))
print_average_check(within_person_average_check(analysis_liberal, within_person_data_liberal$points))
```
